passages.title: My Morning
passages.body: Every morning Maria wakes up at six o’clock. She opens the window and looks at the bright sky. Then she makes a cup of coffee and drinks it slowly. After that she reads a short book for ten minutes. Finally she puts on her shoes and walks to the bus stop. The bus arrives at seven fifteen. She enjoys the quiet time before work.

passages.title: Shopping List
passages.body: Tom writes a shopping list on a piece of paper. He needs three apples, a loaf of bread, two cartons of milk, and a box of cereal. He goes to the store at ten o’clock. In the fruit section he picks the red apples. In the dairy aisle he chooses the fresh milk. He pays at the checkout and walks home. He feels happy with his purchases.

passages.title: At the Park
passages.body: On Saturday morning Alex goes to the park near his house. The grass is green and the trees are tall. He sees a small squirrel running up a tree. He sits on a wooden bench to rest and watches the birds fly. A gentle wind blows and he feels calm. After an hour he stands up and walks back home. He enjoys the quiet afternoon.

passages.title: Anna's Birthday
passages.body: Anna celebrates her sixth birthday with family and friends. The living room is decorated with colorful balloons and a big banner. Her mother bakes a chocolate cake with pink frosting. Everyone sings the happy birthday song and Anna blows out the candles. She opens a gift box and finds a new doll inside. The party ends with laughter and games. She feels very special today.

passages.title: Saturday Market Trip
passages.body: Last Saturday, Anna went to the local market with her brother. They arrived early because the stalls open at nine. Anna bought fresh strawberries, a loaf of bread, and some cheese. Her brother chose a pair of trainers and a blue scarf. After shopping, they sat on a bench and ate an apple each. The weather was sunny but a little windy. They left the market at half past eleven.

passages.title: First Pasta Attempt
passages.body: Yesterday, Marco tried to make a simple pasta dish for the first time. He boiled water, added salt, and put the pasta in. While the pasta cooked, he chopped tomatoes, garlic, and basil. He mixed the vegetables with olive oil in a pan and stirred them for five minutes. When the pasta was ready, he drained it and combined everything in a large bowl. The meal smelled delicious, and Marco felt proud.

passages.title: Seaside Holiday Plans
passages.body: Next month, the Patel family will travel to the seaside. They have booked a small hotel near the beach. Mr Patel wants to swim every morning, while Mrs Patel prefers to read on the sand. Their daughter, Priya, hopes to collect shells, and their son, Rohan, plans to try surfing. The family will leave early on Saturday and return the following Sunday. They are excited about the trip.

passages.title: New Neighbour Lena
passages.body: This morning, a new neighbour moved into the flat next to mine. Her name is Lena and she works as a graphic designer. She brought a large plant and a bright rug. We talked for a few minutes in the hallway. Lena said she likes quiet evenings and often reads before bed. I offered to help her with the heavy boxes, but she smiled and said she was fine.

items.stem: She usually ____ a book every evening before bed.
items.explanation: 'reads' is the third‑person singular present simple form for 'she'. The main distractor 'read' is the base form used with I/you/we/they.

items.stem: There ____ two apples on the kitchen table today.
items.explanation: 'are' agrees with the plural subject 'two apples'. The main distractor 'is' is singular and does not match the plural noun.

items.stem: I usually ____ my homework after school every day.
items.explanation: 'do' is the correct first‑person present simple form. The main distractor 'does' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: The cat often ____ on the sofa in the afternoon.
items.explanation: 'sleeps' is the third‑person singular present simple form for 'the cat'. The main distractor 'sleep' is the base form.

items.stem: We usually ____ to the park on Sundays in the morning.
items.explanation: 'go' matches the first‑person plural subject 'we'. The main distractor 'goes' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: He usually ____ a red car to work every day.
items.explanation: 'has' is the third‑person singular present simple form for 'he'. The main distractor 'have' is the base form used with I/you/we/they.

items.stem: My sister usually ____ pizza for dinner on Fridays.
items.explanation: 'likes' agrees with the third‑person singular subject 'my sister'. The main distractor 'like' is the base form.

items.stem: They usually ____ English at school every weekday morning.
items.explanation: 'study' is the correct base form for the plural subject 'they'. The main distractor 'studies' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: There ____ a pen in my bag right now.
items.explanation: 'is' agrees with the singular noun 'a pen'. The main distractor 'are' is plural.

items.stem: The children often ____ in the garden after school.
items.explanation: 'play' matches the plural subject 'the children'. The main distractor 'plays' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: She usually ____ a new phone every year for her birthday.
items.explanation: 'buys' is the third‑person singular present simple form for 'she'. The main distractor 'buy' is the base form.

items.stem: We usually ____ breakfast at 7 a.m. every morning.
items.explanation: 'eat' is the correct base form for the first‑person plural 'we'. The main distractor 'eats' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: The dog often ____ loudly at night in the house.
items.explanation: 'barks' agrees with the third‑person singular subject 'the dog'. The main distractor 'bark' is the base form.

items.stem: I usually ____ a glass of water before lunch.
items.explanation: 'want' is the correct first‑person present simple form. The main distractor 'wants' is third‑person singular.

items.stem: What does the speaker drink in the morning?
items.audioScript: Good morning. I wake up at seven o’clock. First I brush my teeth. Then I make a cup of coffee. I drink it while I read the news. After that I eat toast with jam. Then I go to work.
items.explanation: The script says the speaker makes a cup of coffee and drinks it.

items.stem: How many apples does the customer buy?
items.audioScript: Excuse me, how much are the apples? They are one pound each. I would like three apples, please. Here you are. That is three pounds. Thank you. The apples look fresh and red. I will eat them for lunch.
items.explanation: The customer asks for three apples and the total is three pounds.

items.stem: Where does the speaker go on Saturday?
items.audioScript: On Saturday I usually go to the park. I walk there with my dog. We play with a ball. In the afternoon I read a book on a bench. Sunday I stay at home and relax.
items.explanation: The speaker says they usually go to the park on Saturday.

items.stem: Which street is the museum on?
items.audioScript: Excuse me, where is the museum? Go straight on this road. Turn left at the traffic lights. The museum is on High Street, next to the library. It opens at ten in the morning.
items.explanation: The directions state the museum is on High Street.

items.stem: What is the speaker's favorite fruit?
items.audioScript: I like many fruits, but my favorite is the orange. It is sweet and juicy. I eat one every day for breakfast. Sometimes I make orange juice. It gives me lots of energy for the morning.
items.explanation: The speaker explicitly says their favorite fruit is the orange.

items.stem: What time does the English class start?
items.audioScript: Our English class is on Monday and Wednesday. It starts at ten o’clock and finishes at eleven thirty. The teacher is Mrs. Brown. We practice speaking and listening. We also do homework after every class.
items.explanation: The script states the class starts at ten o’clock.

items.explanation: Green describes the color of the grass.

items.explanation: They sing the happy birthday song to celebrate Anna's birthday.

items.stem: What is a "cake"?
items.explanation: A cake is a sweet baked food, as described with chocolate and frosting.

items.stem: In the sentence "She eats an apple every morning.", what does "apple" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Apple" refers to a common fruit.

items.stem: In the sentence "He feels happy when he sees his dog.", what does "happy" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Happy" means feeling pleased or glad.

items.stem: In the sentence "I drink a glass of water after lunch.", what does "water" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Water" is a clear, colourless liquid essential for life.

items.stem: In the sentence "The teacher writes on the board.", what does "teacher" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Teacher" is someone who helps others learn.

items.stem: In the sentence "She puts the milk in the fridge.", what does "fridge" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Fridge" is a short form of "refrigerator", a cold storage appliance.

items.stem: In the sentence "He walks to school every morning.", what does "walks" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Walks" means to move by foot, not by vehicle.

items.stem: In the sentence "The cat sleeps on the sofa.", what does "sofa" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Sofa" is another word for a couch, a long upholstered seat.

items.stem: In the sentence "She puts the red apple on the table.", what does "puts" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Puts" means to place something somewhere.

items.stem: Yesterday I ____ my homework quickly before dinner.
items.explanation: The sentence refers to a completed action in the past, so the past simple 'finished' is required. 'Finish' is the base form and does not convey past tense.

items.stem: She ____ to the market early this morning.
items.explanation: The past simple of the irregular verb 'go' is 'went'. 'Go' is the base form and cannot be used for a past event.

items.stem: Can you ____ my cat while I am on holiday?
items.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of someone or something. 'Look for' means to search, which does not fit the context.

items.stem: I didn't go to the party ____ I was feeling ill.
items.explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason for not going. 'So' would indicate a result, which is not the intended meaning.

items.stem: He ____ not finish his project on time.
items.explanation: The past simple negative uses the auxiliary 'did' + 'not'. 'Does' is present tense and cannot be used with a past time marker.

items.stem: Please ____ the lights when you leave the room.
items.explanation: 'turn off' means to switch the lights off; 'turn on' has the opposite meaning.

items.stem: I stayed at home ____ it was raining heavily.
items.explanation: 'because' introduces the reason for staying home; 'so' would indicate a result rather than a cause.

items.stem: My brother usually ____ his bike to work.
items.explanation: 'rides' is the third‑person singular present simple for a habitual action; 'ride' lacks the required -s ending.

items.stem: The movie was not ____ as the book.
items.explanation: The equality comparative uses 'as good as'; 'as better' is ungrammatical.

items.stem: I can't find my keys; I have been ____ them all morning.
items.explanation: 'looking for' means searching; 'looking at' means observing, which does not fit the context.

items.stem: They ____ the film because it was too scary.
items.explanation: 'didn't watch' is the past simple negative appropriate for a completed past decision; 'don't watch' is present tense.

items.stem: Yesterday I ____ to the market and bought some apples.
items.explanation: "went" is the past simple form of "go", matching the past time marker "Yesterday". "go" is the base form, "goes" is third‑person singular present, and "going" is the -ing form, none of which fit a past narrative.

items.stem: Please ____ the lights before you leave the room.
items.explanation: "Turn off" means to switch something off, which fits the instruction to extinguish the lights. "Turn on" would switch them on, "turn up" increases intensity, and "turn down" decreases it.

items.stem: What will the speaker do on Saturday morning?
items.audioScript: Hi, I'm Alex. This weekend I have a few things planned. On Saturday morning I'll visit my grandmother and help her with the garden. In the afternoon I might go for a walk in the park. Sunday is free, so I'll probably just relax at home.
items.explanation: The speaker says he will visit his grandmother on Saturday morning.

items.stem: Where did the speaker find the phone?
items.audioScript: Hey Sam, did you find your phone? Yeah, I looked everywhere. I checked the car, the kitchen table, even my backpack. Finally I found it under the sofa cushions. It was hiding there the whole time.
items.explanation: The speaker states the phone was found under the sofa cushions.

items.stem: Which shirt is cheaper?
items.audioScript: I bought two shirts yesterday. The blue one cost twenty dollars, and the red one cost fifteen dollars. They look similar, but the red one is cheaper. I think I'll wear the red one to work tomorrow.
items.explanation: The red shirt costs fifteen dollars, which is less than the blue shirt's twenty dollars.

items.stem: When did the speaker finish the report?
items.audioScript: Did you finish the report? Yes, I finished it yesterday after lunch. It took me about two hours. Now I can send it to the manager. I'm glad it's done before the deadline. Thanks for asking.
items.explanation: The speaker explicitly says the report was finished yesterday.

items.stem: What does the speaker ask the listener to do?
items.audioScript: Please turn off the TV before you leave the room. The remote is on the coffee table. Thanks. It saves electricity and keeps the house quiet. I'll be back in ten minutes. See you soon.
items.explanation: The speaker directly requests the listener to turn off the TV.

items.stem: What is the speaker going to do after work?
items.audioScript: After work I'm going to meet a friend for coffee. We'll talk about the new project and maybe go for a walk later. It should be a nice evening. I'm looking forward to it. See you there.
items.explanation: The speaker says he is going to meet a friend for coffee after work.

items.explanation: The passage lists strawberries, a loaf of bread, and some cheese as Anna's purchases.

options: Because the stalls open at nine

items.stem: In the passage, the word "windy" means
items.explanation: "Windy" describes weather with a noticeable breeze.

items.explanation: The passage says he chopped tomatoes, garlic, and basil while the pasta cooked.

options: Because he used a new pan

items.stem: The word "drained" in the passage means
items.explanation: To drain pasta is to pour off the cooking water.

items.stem: What does Priya hope to do on the holiday?
items.explanation: The text says Priya hopes to collect shells.

items.stem: In the passage, "excited" means
items.explanation: "Excited" describes a feeling of happy anticipation.

items.stem: What is Lena's job?
items.explanation: The passage explicitly says she works as a graphic designer.

items.stem: Why did the narrator offer to help Lena?
items.explanation: The narrator mentions the heavy boxes as the reason for offering help.

items.stem: The word "bright" describing the rug means
items.explanation: "Bright" here refers to vivid colours.

items.stem: In the sentence "The cake was delicious and everyone asked for the recipe.", what does "delicious" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Delicious" describes food that has a very good flavor, i.e., tasty.

items.stem: In the sentence "After the long walk, Maria felt tired and wanted to rest.", what does "tired" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Tired" means needing sleep or rest; sleepy is a close synonym.

items.stem: In the sentence "The new phone is expensive, so I will wait for a sale.", what does "expensive" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Expensive" means costing a lot of money; costly conveys the same idea.

items.stem: In the sentence "Our neighbour is very friendly and always says hello.", what does "friendly" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Friendly" describes someone who behaves in a kind, pleasant way.

items.stem: In the sentence "He ran quickly to catch the bus.", what does "quickly" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Quickly" means at high speed; fast is a direct synonym.

items.stem: In the sentence "The movie was boring, so we left early.", what does "boring" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Boring" means not interesting; dull carries the same meaning.

items.stem: In the sentence "The sofa is comfortable and perfect for reading.", what does "comfortable" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Comfortable" describes something that gives physical ease; soft is a close synonym.

items.stem: In the sentence "She was excited about the upcoming trip.", what does "excited" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Excited" means feeling strong enthusiasm or happiness about something.

items.stem: I have lived in this city ____ 2015.
items.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time (2015) in present perfect. 'For' requires a duration, 'from' needs 'to', and 'by' indicates a deadline, not a starting point.

items.stem: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ stay at home.
items.explanation: First conditional uses 'will' for a real future possibility. 'Would' belongs to second conditional, while 'can' and 'may' express ability or permission, not the predicted result.

items.stem: If I ____ a million pounds, I would travel the world.
items.explanation: Second conditional requires past simple ('won') after 'if'. 'Win' is present, 'had won' is past perfect, and 'would win' incorrectly mixes conditionals.

items.stem: The book ____ I borrowed from the library was fascinating.
items.explanation: 'Which' refers to things (the book) in a defining relative clause. 'Who' is for people, 'where' for places, and 'whose' shows possession.

items.stem: In my opinion, the new policy ____ improve the situation.
items.explanation: When expressing a personal prediction, 'will' is standard. 'Would' is hypothetical, 'can' indicates ability, and 'may' suggests possibility rather than certainty.

items.stem: We need to ____ a decision before Friday.
items.explanation: The collocation is 'make a decision'. 'Do a decision', 'take a decision' (less common), and 'give a decision' are not standard English collocations.

items.stem: Unless you ____ now, you will miss the train.
items.explanation: After 'unless' we use present simple ('leave') for a future condition. 'Leaves' is third‑person singular, 'leaving' is gerund, and 'left' is past tense.

items.stem: The student ____ essay won the prize is my cousin.
items.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession (the student's essay). 'Who' and 'that' refer to the student, not the essay, and 'which' is for things, not possessive relations.

items.stem: They have ____ finished the report on time.
items.explanation: 'Already' fits affirmative present perfect to indicate completion before now. 'Yet' and 'still' are used in negatives or questions, and 'just' would need 'just finished' without 'have'.

items.stem: If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.
items.explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in the 'if' clause. 'Was' is sometimes heard informally but 'were' is the standard form; 'am' and 'be' are ungrammatical here.

items.stem: This is the café ____ we met for the first time.
items.explanation: 'Where' refers to a place (the café) in a relative clause. 'Which' and 'that' need a preposition ('at which'), and 'when' refers to time, not location.

items.stem: You ____ see a doctor if the pain continues.
items.explanation: 'Should' gives advice, appropriate for a recommendation. 'Must' expresses strong obligation, 'can' ability, and 'might' possibility, which are less suitable for advice.

items.stem: Many students decided to ____ part in the competition.
items.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'take part'. 'Make part', 'do part', and 'give part' are not idiomatic English collocations.

items.stem: She ____ to the new café three times this week.
items.explanation: The present perfect "has been" indicates repeated visits with the speaker still in the present time frame. "Has gone" suggests she is not back, "went" is past simple and does not connect to the present, and "has been going" implies a continuous action rather than completed visits.

items.stem: In the sentence "She managed to finish the project before the deadline.", what does "managed" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Managed" here means she was able to accomplish the task.

items.stem: In the sentence "We should avoid walking alone at night.", what does "avoid" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Avoid" means to keep away from something deliberately.

items.stem: In the sentence "The doctor recommended a daily walk for better health.", what does "recommended" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Recommended" means to suggest something as good or beneficial.

items.stem: In the sentence "Regular exercise can improve your mood.", what does "improve" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Improve" means to make something better or of higher quality.

items.stem: In the sentence "They decided to travel by train instead of flying.", what does "decided" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Decided" means to make a choice after consideration.

items.stem: In the sentence "Could you explain the rules again, please?", what does "explain" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Explain" means to make something understandable or clear.

items.stem: In the sentence "I suggest we meet at the café tomorrow.", what does "suggest" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: "Suggest" means to put forward an idea for consideration.

items.stem: In the sentence "After the meeting, the manager asked the team to summarise the main points before leaving.", what does "summarise" most nearly mean?
items.explanation: Summarise means to give a brief overview of the main points.
